oidc.enabledHelp: Turns the OIDC sign-in button on the login page on or off.
oidc.issuerHelp: Required. The issuer URL of your provider, for example https://auth.example.com/application/o/crosswatch/ for Authentik or https://id.example.com for Pocket ID. CrossWatch reads the provider settings from it.
oidc.clientIdHelp: Required. The client ID of the CrossWatch application at your provider. Set its redirect URI to https://your-crosswatch/api/app-auth/oidc/callback.

provision.title: New logins from OIDC
provision.help: New logins from OIDC: Members of an allowed group get a login and a profile on their first OIDC sign-in. You assign their accounts and pairs afterwards, unless identity matching finds them. Removing them from the group at your identity provider blocks their OIDC sign-in.
provision.createHelp: Off by default. When on, members of an allowed group get a login and an empty profile on their first OIDC sign-in. Needs at least one allowed group.
provision.accessHelp: Access for logins created from OIDC. Full access can change their own data, Read-only can only look. Never administrator. You can change it per login later.
provision.groupsHelp: Required when creating logins. Group names exactly as your provider sends them, separated by commas. Logins created from OIDC are checked against these groups on every sign-in.
provision.groupsClaimHelp: Optional. The claim that holds the group names. Empty uses groups, which Authentik sends by default.
provision.matchHelp: Off by default. When on, a new login gets the identities with the same name on your connections. If a name is not unique, or belongs to another profile, nothing is assigned. Use it only if names on your media servers belong to the same people.
provision.identityClaimHelp: Optional. The claim that holds the media server username, for people whose names differ. Falls back to preferred_username. Users must not be able to edit this claim at your provider.

oidc.linkHelp: Saves the OIDC settings, then opens your provider to link your own OIDC account to this administrator login.

help.webhookUrl:
All events URL:
Use this when one endpoint receives every scheduler event.
CrossWatch sends start, success, and failure to this same http:// or https:// URL with the event in the JSON payload.
help.webhookNotifiarrUrl:
Notifiarr passthrough URL:
Paste the Notifiarr Passthrough endpoint.
CrossWatch sends start, success, and failure notifications to this same URL.
help.webhookNtfyUrl:
ntfy topic URL:
Paste the full topic URL, for example https://ntfy.sh/your-topic.
CrossWatch posts start, success, and failure as plain text with Title and Priority headers.
Start is sent with low priority, success with default priority, and failure with high priority.
help.webhookFormat:
Payload format:
CrossWatch JSON sends the raw scheduler payload.
Notifiarr Passthrough sends the notification/discord JSON shape expected by Notifiarr.
Pushover sends a push notification through the Pushover message API.
ntfy publishes a plain-text notification to an ntfy topic.
help.webhookPushoverToken:
Pushover application token:
The 30 character API token of the application you created in Pushover.
Start is sent with low priority, success with normal priority, and failure with high priority.
help.webhookPushoverUser:
Pushover user key:
The 30 character user key or group key that should receive the notifications.
help.webhookBase:
Compatible base URL:
Use this for Healthchecks.io-style ping.
Paste the base ping URL. CrossWatch sends start to /start, success to the base URL, and failure to /fail.
help.webhookNotifiarrChannel:
Notifiarr channel ID:
Optional Discord channel id for Notifiarr Passthrough payloads.
If your Notifiarr setup requires a channel, enter the numeric Discord channel id here.
help.webhookTimeout:
Timeout seconds:
How long CrossWatch waits for a callback request before logging it as failed.
Callback failures do not fail the sync.
help.webhookStart:
Start callback URL:
Optional explicit http:// or https:// POST destination when a scheduled sync starts.
This overrides the compatible base URL for start events.
help.webhookSuccess:
Success callback URL:
Optional explicit http:// or https:// POST destination when a scheduled sync finishes successfully.
This overrides the compatible base URL for success events.
help.webhookFailure:
Failure callback URL:
Optional explicit http:// or https:// POST destination when a scheduled sync fails.
This overrides the compatible base URL for failure events.
help.webhookAlertWatcher:
Alert when the watcher stops:
Sends watcher_stopped when an enabled watcher route is not running, and watcher_recovered when it runs again.
Each change is sent once. This includes a watcher that was stopped by hand or never started. Turning the watcher source or the route off does not send an alert.
CrossWatch JSON sends these to the All events URL.
help.webhookAlertProviderAuth:
Alert when a provider sign-in is lost:
Sends provider_auth_lost when a provider instance used by an enabled sync pair, watcher route or scrobble webhook needs a new sign-in, and provider_auth_recovered when it works again.
Each change is sent once. A provider that is only unreachable does not send an alert.
CrossWatch JSON sends these to the All events URL.
help.webhookTest:
Send test notification:
Sends one test message with the saved webhook settings.
Save your changes first.
help.webhookAlertUnresolved:
Alert on unresolved items:
Off means only a crashed or aborted run sends the failure callback.
On also sends failure when a run finishes with unresolved items or provider errors, such as a destination rejecting a write. The run itself still counts as successful in CrossWatch.

help.pairPathMatching:
Match by file path
Applies only to this pair. When ID lookup fails, compare file-path endings between Plex, Jellyfin, Emby and Silo.
Supports movies and episodes for history, ratings and progress, including with Strict ID matching enabled. Ambiguous paths and conflicting IDs are skipped.

help.glDry:
Dry run
Plan and log only; no writes. Reset states after testing (in maintenance).
help.glVerify:
Verify after write
Re-check the destination after writes (when supported).
help.glDrop:
Drop guard
Protects against sudden inventory drops by pausing delete plans.
help.glMass:
Allow mass delete
If off, blocks large delete plans (roughly >10%). Enable for first runs.
It's either mass-delete or drop-guard or none; not both.
help.glOnewayRemove:
Deletions based on Source
When enabled, this pair only removes items after CrossWatch observed them disappear from the source.
When disabled, this pair runs mirror mode and removes target items missing from the source (destructive; use with care).
help.glObserved:
Include observed deletes
If off, observed deletes are ignored and delta-delete providers are disabled (safer).
help.glBbEnable:
Blackbox: Enabled
Automatic flapper protection and failure quarantine.
help.glBbPair:
Blackbox: Pair scoped
Keep blackbox decisions per pair instead of global.
help.glBbSection:
Blackbox
Unresolved is only a reporting state: items that fail to write are recorded, shown in diagnostics, and retried on every sync.
Blackbox is the quarantine state and the only thing that stops an item from being planned again.
help.glBbPromote:
Promote after (failed writes)
Number of consecutive failed write attempts before an item is moved to the blackbox.
Until then the item keeps being retried; unresolved alone never blocks it.
help.glSectionMain:
General
Matching and Pair safety apply to this connection. The remaining safety and runtime controls are shared application settings. The defaults are good enough for most users, so only change them when you have a specific reason.
help.glSectionAdvanced:
Advanced
These are extra retention and blackbox safety controls. The defaults are good enough for most users, so you usually do not need to change anything here.

help.cxHsDropped:
Dropped shows
Sync normally: dropped shows sync like any other show.
Ignore dropped: shows dropped on either provider are skipped during history sync. Nothing is removed elsewhere.
Sync + tag dropped: plays of dropped shows still sync, and the show is marked dropped on the other provider. One-way copies the source status to the target, two-way works both ways. SIMKL and WeTrakr keep completed shows as completed. Dropping a show on FlickList also clears its resume points. The CrossWatch tracker keeps the status under My titles, where you can also drop shows yourself. Un-dropping is not synced.
With Status mapping on, use Sync normally: status mapping handles dropped shows, so tagging is turned off.

help.cxPrCwRemovals:
Sync Continue Watching removals (Beta)
When you remove a title from Continue Watching on Emby, Plex, Tofa or Silo, hide it on the other server too. The resume position is kept.
CrossWatch spots a removal when a title leaves the row while its position stays the same, so the first run only takes a snapshot. A title is not hidden when the other side has newer progress. Undoing a removal is not synced.
Tofa and Silo hide a whole show, Emby hides the show's card, Plex hides the episode.
help.cxPrLibraryOnly:
Progress: Only items in destination library
Skip resume positions for movies and episodes that are not in the media server library.
Titles the server already has a position for are always synced.
Matches on IDs only, so titles stored under a different ID are skipped too.
help.cxHsSpecials:
History: Specials (Season 0)
Include Season 0 / specials episodes. Disable to skip them on both sides of this pair.
help.cxHsLibraryOnly:
History: Only items in destination library
Skip movies and episodes that are not in the media server library.
Matches on IDs only, so titles stored under a different ID are skipped too.
help.cxHsUndatedToday:
History: Replace unknown watch dates with today (SIMKL)
When off, explicitly unknown watch dates stay unknown on SIMKL.
Enable this only to replace unknown dates with today on the destination. The source keeps its unknown date. This does not enable unknown-date rewatches.
help.cxHsAllCopies:
History: Update all copies
When the same movie or episode exists more than once on Jellyfin, for example in a regular and a 4K library, every copy is marked as watched instead of just one.
Copies that are still unwatched are filled in too.
Applies to the Jellyfin side of the pair. In two-way pairs between two Jellyfin servers it applies to both.
help.cxHsTraktResets:
History: Follow Trakt rewatch resets
When you start a rewatch of a show on Trakt (Trakt VIP), episodes watched before the reset date are marked unwatched on the media server. Your Trakt history is not changed.
Watches before the reset are not synced in either direction while the reset is active. New watches after the reset sync as usual.
Undoing the reset on Trakt brings the earlier watches back. Off by default.
Needs Trakt VIP. Without VIP nothing is read or changed.
For Plex, reading marked watched items must stay on.
help.cxCoMedia:
Collections: Read from media server
Reads resolution, HDR and audio from the media server and sends them with new collection items.
Adds some extra load on the media server while reading the library.
help.cxCoMediaUpd:
Collections: Update existing items
When the media info of an item changes on the source (for example 1080p to 4K, or a new Atmos track), the item on the destination is updated too.
Only fills in or changes values, never clears them. Physical copies on the destination are left alone.
The first sync can update many items.
help.cxCoCopyDetails:
Collections: Send private copy details
Also send the price, store, shelf, notes and who a copy is lent to.
WeTrakr only shows these to you, but they do leave CrossWatch.
Off by default.
help.cxRtSpecials:
Ratings: Specials (Season 0)
Include Season 0 / specials seasons and episodes. Disable to skip them on both sides of this pair.
help.cxRtLibraryOnly:
Ratings: Only items in destination library
Skip new ratings for movies and episodes that are not in the media server library.
Rating changes for titles you already rated are always synced.
Matches on IDs only, so titles stored under a different ID are skipped too.
help.floppyAnimeLibrary:
Floppy: Send new anime to the Anime library
New anime shows are added to Floppy's Anime library instead of TV Shows.
Only applies to shows Floppy does not have yet. Shows already in Floppy stay in the library they are in.
This setting is per pair.
help.cxJfWlMode:
Jellyfin: Watchlist mode
Jellyfin has no native Watchlist. CrossWatch maps it to:
• Favorites: sets the Favorite flag
• Playlist: writes to a named playlist (episodes only; no shows)
• Collections: writes to a named collection
Changing mode does not move existing items.
Tip: Favorites or Collections are the most compatible.
help.cxEmWlMode:
Emby: Watchlist mode
Emby has no native Watchlist. CrossWatch maps it to:
• Favorites: sets the Favorite flag
• Playlist: writes to a named playlist (episodes only; no shows)
• Collections: writes to a named collection
Changing mode does not move existing items.
Tip: Favorites or Collections are the most compatible.
help.plxMarkedWatched:
Plex: Marked watched
Include watched items from your Plex library, even when no playback-history entry is available. Applies only to this pair.
help.plxCloudRead:
Plex cloud history: Plex to provider
Reads server and account watch history, including titles outside the server libraries. Server library filters do not limit these account-wide cloud reads. In two-way pairs, Read cloud history is independent of Write cloud fallback.
History removals are disabled while enabled. Unavailable cloud reads fail the feature instead of returning partial history. Deleted or unmatchable catalog entries are skipped and counted in the read log. Not supported for managed or switched users.
help.plxDiscoverFallback:
Plex cloud history: Provider to Plex
Writes to your Plex server normally. For missing movies and episodes, uses your Plex account to mark them watched and restore their original watch date. Applies to additions only; existing cloud plays stay unchanged. Rate-limited or unfinished date updates stay unresolved and are retried. In two-way pairs, Write cloud fallback is independent of Read cloud history.
Turning this on turns off Only items in destination library for this pair.
Only for a regular Plex account connected with its own token. Not for managed users or switched Plex Home and shared users.
help.plxWlPms:
Plex watchlist: Allow PMS fallback
The Plex watchlist lives in your Plex account, so CrossWatch first finds each title in the Plex online catalogue (Discover).
When that fails, look the title up by ID in your own Plex server library and add it to the watchlist from there.
Helps for titles that Discover cannot find, but only works for titles that are in your library. Off by default.
help.plxWlTitle:
Plex watchlist: Title text search
When the ID lookup in the Plex online catalogue finds nothing, search it by title, year or slug.
Finds more titles, with a small risk of a wrong match for remakes or titles with the same name.
Turn it off to add titles by ID only; titles without a match then stay unresolved. On by default.
help.plxStrictIds:
Plex: Strict ID matching
When enabled, CrossWatch only matches by IDs (Plex IDs + external IDs). Title/year searches are disabled. The pair Match by file path option can separately enable a file-path fallback.
help.jfStrictIds:
Jellyfin: Strict ID matching
Require Jellyfin or external IDs to confirm matches. Title searches and legacy full-path matching are disabled. The pair Match by file path option can separately enable a file-path fallback.
Episodes can match by series ID plus season and episode numbers.
help.jfTargetedLookup:
Jellyfin: Targeted library lookup
Match through a cached movie and series ID catalogue, then fetch episodes only for matched series.
The catalogue checks for metadata changes on each sync that needs matching and refreshes fully every 24 hours.
Disable to allow a full episode index. Title and path fallback require Strict ID matching to be off.
help.emStrictIds:
Emby: Strict ID matching
When enabled, CrossWatch only matches by IDs (Emby IDs + external IDs). Title/year searches are disabled. The pair Match by file path option can separately enable a file-path fallback.
help.siloStrictIds:
Silo: Strict ID matching
On by default. Only match by TMDB, IMDb or TVDB IDs. Turn it off to also match by title: movies by title and year, shows by title and episodes by show title plus season and episode number. A title must point to exactly one Silo item and must not contradict known IDs. The pair Match by file path option can separately enable a file-path fallback.
